A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GBSM study. Their main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F report original Garnet MDP experiments comparing policy-transfer regret and aggregation/estimation errors with theoretical bounds.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain original Garnet experiments and additionally report value-function approximation results.

M1.justification: The GBSM recursion, policy-transfer mapping, aggregation and sampling constructions, and lax/on-policy variants remain unchanged. The value-function approximation additions concern guarantees and evaluation of these existing constructions.

E1.justification: V3 adds evaluation of value-function approximation under aggregation, alongside policy transfer and state-similarity approximation. This is a limited extension of task coverage within the same synthetic Garnet MDP family.

E2.justification: The aggregation comparisons in Figures 1b and 5–7 drop v1's 2σ̃/(1−γ) comparator attributed to Kemertas and Aumentado-Armstrong. The new VFA comparisons use a bound with that formula attributed to Zhang et al. Song et al.'s transfer measure and Ferns et al.'s SSA comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added VFA evaluation compares maximum absolute optimal-value differences with their bounds. Retained experiments keep the stated 20 states, five actions, 50% branching, half-state aggregation, Gaussian noise standard deviations of 0.1–0.3, and discount-factor grid.

E4.justification: Appendix F extends the discount-factor sweep to VFA in Figures 11–13, examining bound tightness across γ=0.1 through 0.9. The existing policy-transfer and state-similarity approximation sweeps remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 independent experiments per discount factor and plot individual trials. V3 introduces no change in run-count reporting, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing.

E6.justification: V3 adds a full family of VFA bound-versus-ground-truth outcomes in Figure 1d and Figures 11–13, while plotted trial values also change throughout the retained comparisons in Figures 2–10. This substantially revises the reported empirical results, although the main bound-tightness conclusions persist. The PDFs do not establish performance gains on identical random instances.

T1.justification: V3 adds an explicit optimal-policy VFA bound in Theorem 4.4 and a nonoptimal-policy counterpart in Theorem E.3, extending existing value-difference and aggregation arguments. V1's aggregation and sampling theorems survive as Theorems 4.5 and 4.6; the foundational metric properties and sample-complexity result remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution summary and conclusion retain the claims of three GBSM properties, tighter multi-MDP bounds and explicit sample complexity. The new VFA material develops the existing approximation contribution without changing these headline claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 now distinguishes state-similarity approximation from value-function approximation and clarifies which error quantity each comparison addresses. Section 5 explicitly connects the extension to nonoptimal-policy value approximation. The discounted-versus-average-reward limitation and proposed applications remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The documented Garnet construction, aggregation/noise settings and tabular Q-learning description are retained. V3 adds no implementation, hardware, timing or code/data-access disclosure.

R1.justification: V3 adds Zhang et al.'s representation-learning work and distinguishes its optimal-policy VFA bound from Kemertas and Aumentado-Armstrong's nonoptimal-policy result. The latter reference is retained, moving from reference 6 to reference 15. Broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites introduce SSA/VFA terminology and reorganize Section 4.2 around VFA followed by SSA. The introduction and experimental explanation are adjusted, while the overall section structure and most prose and proofs remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from three to four panels, and Appendix F adds Figures 11–13 for VFA. Existing plots retain their format with revised legends, labels and scales. Figures 9–10 introduce caption errors: they say aggregation although their axes identify estimation.

improvement.justification: V3 improves scientific clarity by separating state-similarity and value-function approximation and aligning their bound comparisons in Section 4.2. The explicit VFA bounds and numerical validation provide a useful extension of the retained framework. The new caption errors in Figures 9–10 are a limited drawback that does not outweigh these gains.
